chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu Saeed al-Qammat, from Dawud ibn Kathir, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: My father (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Any two Muslims who desert each other, and remain so for three days not reconciling, except that they both would have exited from Islam, and there would be no Wilayah between them. So whichever of the two preceded to speak to his brother, he would precede him to Paradise on the Day of Reckoning.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on two Muslims who stop speaking to each other for three days?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi emphasizes the severity of prolonged estrangement (hijr) between Muslims, linking social cohesion to spiritual standing. While the phrase 'exited from Islam' is interpreted by Shia scholars as a loss of specific relational bonds rather than apostasy, the reward for initiating reconciliation highlights the virtue of humility and peace-making. The narration underscores that mending ties is not merely a social courtesy but a decisive factor in one's ultimate spiritual success.
